verdict: PayPal moved $464B of payments (+11%) and grew revenue 7% to $8.4B, but net profit fell 14% to $1.1B as transaction costs rose faster than revenue and its investment portfolio swung to a loss.

segments.name: Transaction revenues
segments.note: The cut PayPal takes on every payment it processes — $464B of payment volume flowed through in the quarter, up 11%, across 6.5 billion transactions.

segments.name: Revenues from other value added services
segments.note: Interest on customer balances, partner fees and other services around the core payment.

flow.costPlain: What each payment costs PayPal to run: $4,165M of transaction expense (card-network and processing fees) plus $378M of transaction and credit losses on its loans.

opex.name: Customer support and operations
opex.note: Support staff and the cost of running payment operations.

opex.name: Sales and marketing
opex.note: Marketing, and winning merchants and users.

opex.name: Technology and development
opex.note: Building and running the PayPal and Venmo platforms.

opex.name: General and administrative
opex.note: Running the company: finance, legal, risk and offices.

opex.name: Restructuring and other
opex.note: Severance and reshaping costs as PayPal works through its transformation plan.

takeaways.title: The payment pipes keep growing
takeaways.text: Total payment volume rose 11% to $464.0B and transactions rose 7% to 6.5 billion, with 439 million active accounts.

takeaways.title: Growth picked up a little
takeaways.text: Revenue grew 7%: transaction revenues +7% and value-added services +10%. U.S. revenue rose 9% while international revenue grew 4%.

takeaways.title: Shareholders are getting the cash
takeaways.text: PayPal returned $1.5B to shareholders via buybacks in the quarter — $6.0B over twelve months — funding the returns from its cash pile even as GAAP profit fell.

oneTimers: GAAP results include $101M of losses on PayPal's strategic investment portfolio (inside other expense), versus gains a year ago — a swing that explains much of the profit decline.
Restructuring and other charges were $74M in the quarter as new leadership simplifies the organization.
otherDetail: Other income (expense), net was −$95M, including $101M of losses on PayPal's strategic investment portfolio.
